definition: A sensory area is a brain region mainly involved in processing incoming sensory information, often at a relatively basic level such as visual features. The source also indicates that such areas can sometimes respond to input from other senses or to higher-level signals like spoken language.

reasons: The packet supports this description for primary visual cortex (V1), but the definition generalizes from that single example to sensory areas in general without support.
The claim that sensory areas can respond to other senses or spoken language is supported only for V1 in this source, not established as a general property of sensory areas.

The definition makes a broad, category-level claim (“A sensory area is a brain region mainly involved…”) that is not directly stated or substantiated in the packet, which only discusses primary visual cortex (V1) specifically.

While the packet supports that V1 can process basic visual features and show multisensory effects and activation by spoken language, it does not establish a general definition of “sensory area” beyond V1 (e.g., as a general type of brain region across the brain).
